purpose: Define candidate field meanings and ownership boundaries before any Velvet Factory printer facts are made canonical.
principles: Core may own generic schemas/interfaces/algorithms; it must not own Velvet Factory fleet facts.
Instance owns verified local printer/profile/business bindings.
Secrets/private identifiers stay outside public Instance config.
Transient telemetry/queue/active-job state belongs to an approved runtime state store, not Git.
No field in this draft authorizes printer upload, start, control or automatic scheduling.
Unknown values remain unknown; do not infer model capability from marketing or memory.

field_inventory.meaning: stable local logical printer identity
verified manufacturer name
verified model designation
verified fabrication process such as FFF/FDM; enum defined by future Core schema
verified usable build volume; never copied from an unverified listing
verified installed tool/extruder count
verified supported/installed nozzle sizes as scoped by evidence
verified supported material classes under local profiles; no quality claim
verified physical enclosure state/capability
verified heated-bed capability
verified local multi-material/tool-changing mode, if any
verified slicer/tool routes allowed by current fabrication authority
references to verified local print/slicer profiles
source/receipt references supporting each capability claim
last verification time for the scoped fact set
evidence state; not a marketing-quality score
local operator-friendly identifier
advisory local use tags; not an authorization gate
device identifier; do not place in public config
local/network addressing; never public by default
pointer only; credentials never stored in this registry
current maintenance/availability state if a verified provider exists
current job reference only when live evidence exists
current production queue state from canonical operations source
provider observation time; absence is not offline proof

core_responsibilities: define generic field schema and validation
define advisory scheduling algorithms that accept Instance facts as input
instance_responsibilities: hold verified fleet values and profile bindings
hold local supplier/business bindings where applicable
supply current facts explicitly to Core algorithms
keep sensitive/private values in the appropriate private/secret source

rollout_sequence.name: verified_registry
rollout_sequence.requirement: establish evidence-backed fleet facts before optimization

rollout_sequence.name: incident_records
rollout_sequence.requirement: record print/process incidents and corrective/effectiveness evidence

rollout_sequence.name: advisory_capacity
rollout_sequence.requirement: produce advisory scenarios only from verified capability and demand inputs

rollout_sequence.name: automatic_scheduling
rollout_sequence.requirement: out of scope until later explicit authority, evidence and safety gates exist

advisory_capacity_inputs.source: verified job/slicer evidence or explicit unknown

incident_method_notes.capa: Generic root-cause → corrective action → effectiveness verification may be adapted. Medical/regulatory CAPA obligations are excluded.
incident_method_notes.fmea: Generic failure-mode/probability/severity/control framing may be adapted. ISO 14971 compliance claims and unverified numeric thresholds are excluded.

verification_design.schema: future Core schema validates type/ownership/sensitivity but never supplies VF values
verification_design.instance: every capability value carries evidence and verification state
verification_design.privacy: public Instance projection excludes private/secret/runtime-state classes
negative_controls: no business facts in generic Core defaults

rollback: Remove the Stage 8 adapter/schema and keep current vfprod/instance sources unchanged; compatibility reads must exist before any future migration removes legacy fields.
